transcript: I'm Assuming You Know David Greenspan, or maybe you don't, like I didn't, but either way, I think you'll enjoy this play. In an ironic turn for Atlantic Theater Company, this play is largely about how impossible it is to make a living working in the theater. If the irony isn't clear, go look up why Atlantic had to postpone this show in January. Anyway, this is a solo piece written by Mona Pirnot starring David Greenspan in which he plays both the narrator, directly taking on the point of view of the playwright Mona, and numerous characters in a story about playwriting and David Greenspan himself. I don't wanna give too much away about this piece because its cleverness is best if not spoiled, but I would absolutely recommend it. It’s so funny, the way David Greenspan assumes different voices and physicalities, and the fluidity with which he holds scenes with just himself is really cool. And the play itself is also very cool — it's meta and self-referential in a really humorous but earnest way, with multiple layers of storytelling and commentary happening simultaneously. I loved the way the whole piece unfolded, but even within the first few minutes I knew it was going to be fantastic. I'm Assuming You Know David Greenspan is only running through the end of April. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: Creator explicitly recommends, praises Greenspan's performance and the play's cleverness, and says they knew it would be fantastic within minutes.
